title: Check @OnStart methods when the class is read

blocks.text: The page's best practice: **validate annotations early**, at startup, not while requests are being served, and give **meaningful error messages**. A framework that finds a broken `@OnStart` method only when the first bean is started fails in production; one that checks when it reads the class fails at boot, with every problem listed.

items: `CallbackPlan.of(Class<?> type)` reads the `@OnStart` methods that `type` declares (any access level). An `@OnStart` method must take no parameters; if any takes some, `of` throws `IllegalArgumentException` **at once, before any bean exists**, and its message names **every** such method.
`names()` returns the callbacks' names in run order: lowest `order` first.
`run(Object bean)` calls the callbacks on `bean` in that order.

rows: seven callbacks with orders 0 to 6, declared in another order

cases.says: A plan for Cache names its seven callbacks lowest order first (allocate, open, warmUp, announce, load, index, report; any access level) and runs them in that order on each bean.
CallbackPlan.of(Broken.class) itself throws IllegalArgumentException, before any bean is run.
The message names both open(String) and load(int), and not the valid ready().

concepts: Annotations are validated at startup, not during request processing, with error messages that say what is wrong.
